bw: Painful hand spasm only while writing
w: A wrist splint does not treat a task-specific dystonia.
SSRIs treat anxiety or depression, not focal dystonia.
p: Writer's cramp is a task-specific focal dystonia; botulinum toxin injections into the affected muscles are first-line therapy.

w: A cerebellopontine angle tumor causes progressive hearing loss with persistent imbalance, not episodes lasting hours.
AICA occlusion causes sudden vertigo with facial weakness and sensorineural hearing loss.
p: Meniere disease: endolymphatic hydrops causing episodic vertigo, tinnitus, aural fullness and fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss; treat with salt restriction and diuretics.

bw: Lip swelling and vesicles after orthodontic wire
w: Herpes labialis presents as grouped vesicles on the vermilion border with prodromal tingling.
Dermatitis herpetiformis causes grouped pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces and is linked to celiac disease.
p: Nickel in orthodontic appliances commonly causes type IV allergic contact dermatitis of lips and oral mucosa.

x: truncated; polycythemia vera also JAK2 positive

bw: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections, greasy loose stools
w: Cystic fibrosis causes metabolic alkalosis from salt loss, not acidosis.
Anti-GAD antibodies belong to type 1 diabetes, not cystic fibrosis.
p: Cystic fibrosis causes fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption (vitamin K deficiency raises PT), pancreatic insufficiency and recurrent pulmonary infections.

w: An ECG does not explain Kussmaul breathing and altered mentation.
Abdominal CT delays diagnosis and treatment of the metabolic emergency.
p: Kussmaul respirations with abdominal pain and confusion suggest diabetic ketoacidosis; a fingerstick glucose is the fastest first test.

w: Parotidectomy is not needed for acute suppurative parotitis.
Duct dilation treats sialolithiasis or stricture, not acute bacterial infection.
p: Acute suppurative parotitis (S. aureus, anaerobes) occurs in dehydrated or postoperative patients; give IV antibiotics, hydration and sialogogues.

bw: Itchy papules in axillae and groin
w: Nystatin treats candidal infections, which have satellite pustules and no burrows.
Hydrocortisone relieves itch but does not kill the mites.
p: Scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei): treat with topical permethrin on the whole body and treat contacts; ivermectin for crusted or immunosuppressed patients.

w: Amniotic fluid embolism occurs during labor or delivery with sudden collapse and DIC.
Pulmonary thromboembolism causes pleuritic pain and hypoxia without crackles or hypertension.
p: Preeclampsia can cause pulmonary edema from capillary leak and increased afterload; treat with diuretics, antihypertensives and magnesium.

w: The apnea test comes only after the brainstem reflexes are absent.
EEG is an ancillary test, not a first step in brain death determination.
p: Brain death determination: exclude confounders, then test brainstem reflexes, then do the apnea test; ancillary tests only if these cannot be completed.

bw: Foot drop, sensory loss over dorsum and first web space
w: Eversion is lost in common peroneal palsy because the peroneal muscles are paralyzed.
Hip flexion (femoral nerve) is unaffected, so weakness would point elsewhere.
p: Common peroneal neuropathy (fibular head compression): foot drop, weak dorsiflexion and eversion, normal inversion (tibial nerve).

bw: Narrow mediastinum, no response to oxygen
w: Lithium causes Ebstein anomaly, which gives cardiomegaly with a boxy heart, not an egg-shaped silhouette.
Maternal hypothyroidism is not linked to transposition of the great arteries.
p: Poorly controlled maternal diabetes raises the risk of transposition of the great arteries (egg on a string), macrosomia, hypoglycemia and caudal regression.
